agree.reason: A rubric-driven judge gets a clear need, a costed plan with matched funds, and reporting commitments in under ten minutes, though a sceptical reader may notice the hiring timeline doesn't add up.

honest.reason: The brief asked for a third attorney, but the document recasts the grant as refilling a departing attorney's post and asserts 'we have no other funding to refill her position,' which the brief never states. The 'one attorney could represent about 80 a year' figure also treats an open caseload as an annual count.

works_the_facts.reason: It correctly works out about one in three (163 of 463 who asked), roughly 380 turned away, the $13,000 gap and 83% coverage that doesn't depend on the county, and it puts each figure in a favourable but true form.

right_comparison.reason: The no-grant alternative of one attorney and more tenants turned away is drawn concretely, but it rests on the unsupported claim that there is no other funding, and it says nothing about what losing the county contract would do to the clinic.

qualification.reason: The county renewal is dated (October) and its effect on this grant is defused by the 83% figure, and the comparison data has a January start, but there is no date for when results will be reported and no consequence stated if the clerk's data doesn't come.

objections.reason: It meets the missing-comparison and county-risk objections well. It ignores the obvious one that a May decision plus a five-month hiring history makes the promised handover training before the June departure implausible.

fit.reason: At about 290 words with a title and signature, it fits the 300-word project summary format cleanly.
